sections.content: How many people stayed in Torpoint after gaining qualifications?

Torpoint is a small town in the South West. Torpoint does not have its own university.

Torpoint has higher levels of deprivation.

Overall, Torpoint ended up with:

  • fewer non-graduates with advanced qualifications than it produced
Note: all towns and cities in this analysis are defined based on population size only. This means that some cities are classed as towns because of their population.

Let's explore this further

There were 435 state-school pupils from Torpoint who sat their GCSEs between the 2007 to 2008 and the 2010 to 2011 school years.

Of these, 125 (29%) went on to gain degree-level qualifications (level 6+ as defined by The Office of Qualifications and Examinations Regulation, or Ofqual ). We will call these people graduates.

Another 165 (38%) went on to gain other advanced post-16 qualifications, such as A-Levels, a foundation degree or higher apprenticeship (levels 3-5 as defined by Ofqual). In this tool, we will refer to these non-graduates with advanced qualifications as “qualified non-graduates", for brevity.

The charts below compare Torpoint to other English towns and cities using three measures:

  • what proportion of Torpoint's pupils became graduates or qualified non-graduates by the 2017 to 2018 academic year
  • of those graduates and qualified non-graduates, the percentages that lived in Torpoint in the 2018 to 2019 academic year
  • how many graduates and qualified non-graduates from elsewhere came to live there by 2018 to 2019, relative to the number who sat their GCSEs there

In some towns, some of this information may not be available because of small sample sizes.
The size and deprivation level of a town, as well as the qualification levels of older residents, were all related to students' educational attainment. Read our previous analysis.

Where did those who left Torpoint move to?

Of Torpoint's graduates, 75 were living elsewhere in 2018/19.

However, 25 of those graduates (33%) were living fairly locally, in the Plymouth travel to work area (TTWA).

Of Torpoint's qualified (level 3+) non-graduates, 55 were living elsewhere in 2018/19.

However, 30 of those qualified non-graduates (55%) were living fairly locally, in the Plymouth travel to work area (TTWA).

Of those in Torpoint's GCSE cohort:

  • 35 graduates left the South West

In 2018 to 2019, 19% of qualified non-graduates living in Torpoint had moved there from elsewhere

In the 2018 to 2019 academic year, there were 130 qualified (level 3+) non-graduates from our cohort living in Torpoint, compared with the 165 qualified non-graduates who had lived there when they sat their GCSEs.

In the 2018 to 2019 academic year, 81% of qualified (level 3+) non-graduates in Torpoint had also lived there when they sat their GCSEs, while 19% had moved there from elsewhere.
